bullets.title: AI bubble under pressure: High-beta momentum factor down 26% in one month
bullets.body: Nasdaq is down ~9% from its October peak, underperforming equal-weight S&P 500 by 12%, as AI capex ROI and monetization concerns dominate. High-Beta Momentum peaked June 22 at +69% YTD and has collapsed 26% in the last month; SOXX broke below July lows and is down ~21% month-over-month. GS Prime reports Global Fundamental L/S lost 12.6% in October with US Info Tech seeing its largest notional net selling since June, and the long/short ratio at just 1.71 (7th percentile over 5 years).

bullets.title: 22V Research: AI earnings mentions not broadening; $7T capex thesis lacks foundation
bullets.body: AI usage among S&P companies is down quarter-over-quarter with no broadening across sectors; 65% of companies lump AI into vague savings comments. 37 AI Quantifiers guided to only 60bps of margin improvement this quarter vs. 130bps last quarter, and 57% of enterprises remain in pilot/testing phase vs. production. The $7T AI capex buildout thesis requires productivity gains diffusing across the whole economy, which the data does not yet support.

bullets.title: NVDA restricts China exposure; orders partners to limit Chinese customer sales to <49%
bullets.body: Nvidia instructed data center clients/partners to make at least 51% of AI infrastructure service sales to non-Chinese companies, a new and material restriction on China exposure. This follows Hedgeye flagging NVDA in "Quad4 Crash Mode," down 15.4% from ATH, with bearish TRADE and TREND signals. ALAB also reportedly received China restraint orders.

bullets.title: Geopolitical escalation: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island; crude firms; parties far from deal
bullets.body: The U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island overnight; Iran reports three oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. A senior Iranian official stated the two sides remain far apart on any deal. WTI is up ~1.7% to $97.91 and Brent crude traded modestly higher after its largest single-day decline since April 8. UBS softlines note flags Iran conflict endgame as a potential turning point for retail positioning.

bullets.title: Pre-market tape: semis outperform; software/large-cap tech under pressure
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures are roughly flat to slightly positive (~+0.15% to 7563.5) while Nasdaq 100 futures are up ~0.4%; 10-year yield is +3bps to 4.93%. SOXX is up ~2.5-2.8% as AEHR (+16%), AEIS (+12%), and LSCC (+11%) lead on earnings beats, while software (IGV) is -1.5%. Risk Control strategies are expected to turn buyers today after heavy systematic selling, with flows settling ahead of midterms.

bullets.title: AAPL misses on Services and gross margin; memory cost inflation flagged as 'unprecedented'
bullets.body: Apple's F4Q EPS beat on iPhone/Mac strength, but F1Q27 Services guidance of 8-9% growth badly missed consensus of ~12%, with the deceleration driven by App Store model changes, US link-out rules, and mobile gaming weakness. Gross margin guidance of 45-46% missed consensus of ~46.6-46.9% as management described memory cost inflation as "unprecedented" and worsening; Siri AI inference adds another cost layer. AAPL China sales of $17.54B missed the $18.75B expectation. Multiple sell-side firms note the stock was priced at ~35x for perfection it didn't deliver; GS cut PT to $380 from $390.

bullets.title: Enterprise IT survey: AI still in pilot phase; net new spend sentiment at lowest since 2016
bullets.body: A 347-buyer enterprise IT survey shows 56% of buyers cite AI as top new-software spending priority (up 22pts YoY), but 57% remain in pilot/testing vs. only 7% fully deployed. Net 4Q spending sentiment fell to 6% from 19%, the lowest reading since 2016, and 66% expect flat subscriber counts next year, limiting seat-led expansion. MSFT and ORCL are seen as best positioned; broad software sector faces deceleration and valuation pressure despite the AI narrative. AI-driven software reacceleration is widely expected to be deferred to 2028 as customers complete ROI validation.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples contracting: IGV -1.3% YTD vs S&P +11.7%; All-SaaS index at 5.8x FY+2
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index contracted 6.3% week-over-week to 5.8x FY+2 EV/Sales; All-Security multiples contracted 5.7% to 8.8x. IGV has returned -1.3% YTD vs the S&P 500's +11.7%. Broad software positioning is unwinding while beaten-down names (CPNG, GRAB, SRAD, DKNG, FLUT, app software) are up 10-15% in two sessions on short covering.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers issued $271B in debt YTD; AI monetization by 2028 key to avoiding ratings pressure
bullets.body: Hyperscalers have already exceeded GS's full-year $250B debt issuance forecast with $271B issued YTD. META is seeking a $20B bond offering; ORCL raised ~$10B in bonds plus ~$10B in equity (secondary priced at $116/share for 86.2M shares) for AI capex. GS flags AI monetization by 2028 as the key variable that would limit ratings agency pressure.

bullets.title: Marvell acquires Lumentum for $115B all-stock; Jensen Huang blessed deal pre-announcement
bullets.body: Marvell announced a definitive agreement to acquire Lumentum at $1,132/share (23.9% premium to Oct 28 price), representing ~$115B EV — the largest semiconductor acquisition on record. LITE shareholders receive 4.5 MRVL shares per share; deal targets $1B+ annual run-rate cost synergies and is expected to close 1H 2028. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly approved the deal before it was announced publicly. The primary strategic rationale is vertical integration of DSPs, switches, and silicon photonics with lasers/optical components to compete in Scale Up/Scale In GPU/XPU roadmaps. CIEN fell 11.3% on the news as it buys key lasers from LITE; COHR's optical assets gained scarcity value. MRVL was downgraded to hold/neutral at both TD Cowen (PT $350→$175) and BofA (PT $400→$225).

bullets.title: Data center capacity projected to grow from 136 GW to 316 GW by 2030 (~20% CAGR)
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley models global data center capacity nearly doubling from 136 GW in 2026 to 316 GW by 2030 despite headwinds from inflation, financing costs, and political risk. AMZN secured ~$80B in vendor financing (likely NVDA) through Q3 2028, reducing near-term equity/debt needs. Power, politics, and pricing are the key variables shaping the build-out trajectory.

bullets.title: Tech vol elevated: VIX +2.8pts to 21.2; SMH 1M implied vol at 77th percentile
bullets.body: VIX rose 2.8 points to 21.2 driven by a rise in S&P 500 constituent implied correlation. SMH 1M implied vol is at the 77th percentile with put-call skew at 1-year highs, signaling bearish hedging. Bond vol is also elevated with LQD 1M implied vol at the 92nd percentile and flat term structures indicating rate path uncertainty. APP 1M implied vol jumped 15.9pts to 95.5 (98th percentile) ahead of its Nov 4 earnings print.

bullets.title: Post-midterm seasonality historically bullish: S&P has never closed lower at 6M and 12M horizons
bullets.body: Jefferies notes the S&P 500 has never closed lower 6 or 12 months after U.S. midterm elections, with an average 12% gain at the 6-month mark. Risk Control strategies are estimated to turn buyers today after heavy systematic selling, providing a potential near-term technical tailwind.

bullets.title: ON beat-and-raise: AI data center revenue $180M (+160% y/y); expects $620M in 2026 and doubling again in 2027
bullets.body: Onsemi reported Q3 EPS of $0.90 vs. consensus $0.88, with AI data center revenue disclosed for the first time at $180M (+160% y/y). Management guided to ~$620M AI data center revenue in 2026 (+140% y/y) and expects another doubling to ~$1.25B in 2027 (~15% of sales). ON also acquired Ferric Semiconductor for $600M cash plus $175M contingent to strengthen AI power solutions. Multiple sell-side firms cut PTs on multiple compression (Citi to $80 from $98) despite raising EPS estimates.

bullets.title: France fiscal deterioration: 2026 deficit forecast raised to 5.5% of GDP on 0.3% growth
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its France 2026 general government deficit forecast to 5.5% of GDP (from 5.4%), following a 3Q GDP print showing 0.5% annualized contraction that dragged the full-year growth outlook to just 0.3%. The 2027 deficit forecast was also raised to 5.3%, with structural primary balance consolidation averaging only 0.6%-pt over 2026-27, slower than the 2025 pace.

bullets.title: Disney targeting 20% annual cost cuts; likely to trigger thousands of layoffs
bullets.body: Disney is asking managers to reduce costs by 20%, a move that is expected to trigger thousands of layoffs across its operations. This is consistent with a broader pattern of media-sector restructuring as streaming profitability pressure continues.

bullets.title: AI adoption accelerating in corporate sector but CFOs shifting to lower-cost models
bullets.body: Ramp data shows ~55% of US businesses now spending on AI (vs. lower government estimates), and companies spending $30+ per employee monthly hired ~12% more workers than non-adopters. However, CFOs are increasingly scrutinizing expensive frontier models and shifting toward lower-cost alternatives; AI inference has emerged as a major corporate expense category, up 21x year-over-year. AI-spending companies doubled revenue over 3 years vs. ~10% growth for low adopters.

bullets.title: Korea KOSPI down 38% from June peak; Asia showing moderate tech risk aversion
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell 3.6% overnight and is now down 38% from its June peak, consistent with a broader deterioration in global tech sentiment. Korea's exports serve as a leading indicator for US goods demand, adding macro significance to the move. Asia broadly is showing moderate risk aversion for tech equities while Europe is in a rotational bear market with selective earnings strength.

bullets.title: PLTR strong quarter but shorter sovereign AI contracts compress RPO/backlog metrics
bullets.body: Palantir reported its 13th consecutive quarter of accelerating revenue growth at +96% y/y, with US Commercial revenue surpassing US Government for the first time ($3.94B run-rate, +148% y/y). However, US Commercial TCV bookings slowed sharply to +11% y/y from +153% last quarter, and RPO/backlog were sequentially flat for the first time since 1Q23 — attributed to shorter-duration Sovereign AI contracts. Stock fell 6-8% post-earnings despite the operational beat.

bullets.title: CRM acquires Cresta for $2.7B; ORCL raises $20B to fund AI infrastructure
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring AI contact center startup Cresta for $2.7B to strengthen voice agent capabilities. Oracle raised approximately $20B through a combination of a secondary share sale at $116/share (86.2M shares) and bond offerings to fund AI infrastructure buildout. Both moves underscore the accelerating enterprise AI capex cycle despite investor skepticism about near-term ROI.
